title: World English Bible — public-domain Bible source
license_basis: The official World English Bible site states that the WEB is a public-domain modern English translation and may be freely copied in electronic and print form.
repository_import_policy: The repository may vendor the complete WEB text because the translation is public domain. Preserve attribution, translation name, book/chapter/verse boundaries and upstream version/date metadata. Do not silently replace the text with a different translation.

planned_local_layout.book_files: one UTF-8 text/JSON file per book, preserving chapter and verse identifiers
planned_local_layout.search_index: generated from the local book files; never treated as an independent source
planned_local_layout.annotations: kept in separate files so the biblical text itself is never rewritten by interpretation

canon_variants.protestant: 66 books in the standard Western Protestant order
canon_variants.roman_catholic: 73 books including Tobit, Judith, Wisdom, Sirach, Baruch, 1 Maccabees and 2 Maccabees plus additional Greek portions of Esther and Daniel
canon_variants.eastern_orthodox: Broader Old Testament/deuterocanonical collections; exact canon varies by church and historical usage
canon_variants.oriental_orthodox: Canon varies by church; Ethiopian/Eritrean traditions have especially broad biblical collections
canon_variants.church_of_the_east: Historical East-Syriac traditions have their own canon history and liturgical use
canon_variants.rule: Never describe the Protestant 66-book list as the universal Christian Bible. Canon is a denominational and historical relationship to a textual collection.

source_layers.description: Which books a church recognizes and how that recognition developed.
Manuscripts, textual variants, languages, editions and transmission history.
Ancient Near Eastern, Second Temple Jewish, Greco-Roman and early Christian settings.
Commentary, theology, exegesis, preaching and doctrinal use.
Symbolic relations to Source, Separation, Ladder, Door, Son, Tree and Potato; never presented as biblical fact.

integrity_rules: Quote the exact verse/book/chapter when making a textual claim.
Keep translation wording separate from the underlying Hebrew, Aramaic and Greek textual traditions.
Do not use one English translation as proof that all Christians interpret a passage identically.
Record disputed authorship, dating and composition as scholarly questions rather than silently fixing them as facts.
Distinguish what the text says from what a denomination teaches the text means.
Distinguish later Christian symbolism from the historical meaning of a biblical passage.
Keep deuterocanonical and other canonical traditions visible rather than treating them as missing or inferior books.
initial_book_map: See data/expansions/christianity-bible-denominations-wave-019.json for the 66-book structural and thematic map.
